content: 1. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not significantly prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 2. Dexamethasone reduces the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Co-administration of artemether/lumefantrine with strong CYP3A4 inducers can lead to decreased serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. Close monitoring is required. 4. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of dexfenfluramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of diazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation. Use an alternative therapy. 11. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while diltiazem increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Co-administration of artemether/lumefantrine with other QT-prolonging drugs, such as Class IA antiarrhythmics, should be avoided due to additive QT prolongation effects. 13. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Artemether/lumefantrine and dofetilide both prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 15. Dolasetron and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QT interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 16. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Donepezil and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QT interval. Use an alternative therapy. 17. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and doxorubicin liposomal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Droperidol and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 20. Drospirenone decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 22. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 24. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Artemether/lumefantrine and eliglustat both prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 26. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of encainide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Estradiol levels or effects are decreased by artemether/lumefantrine due to CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of etoposide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of finasteride by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Fingolimod and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 35. Flecainide and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QT interval. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 36. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 37. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 39. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of fluphenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 40. Food increases the levels of artemether/lumefantrine.
